name: Resilient and Connected Appalachians Grant Program
summary: Grants of up to USD 100,000 for land and easement acquisition projects that permanently conserve climate-resilient, connected lands in the Appalachians. The third annual round has closed.

eligibility.rule: Land trust, conservation 501(c)(3), nonprofit academic body, eligible public body, or federal Tribe or its nonprofit
Project is within TNC's Appalachians Program boundary
Permanently protects land within or intersecting the Resilient and Connected Network
Intersects a mapped focal area, or qualifies for exceptional consideration near one
Parcels share ownership. Non-adjacent parcels have a conservation relationship that promotes landscape connectivity.
Project closes on or after April 1, 2027
Applicant submits only one application per year
Project closes within 12 months from the start of the grant agreement term

documents: Project budget, including budget worksheet and narrative
Conflict Inquiry form, if a nonprofit
Current LTAC accreditation letter, for land trusts maintaining accreditation through 2027
Accreditation letter of intent submitted within the past year, if applicable to a non-accredited nonprofit
IRS determination letter for non-accredited land trusts and other nonprofits
Bylaws and articles of incorporation for non-accredited land trusts and other nonprofits
Latest Form 990 or financial statement for non-accredited land trusts and other nonprofits
Home-state Certificate of Good Standing for non-accredited land trusts and other nonprofits

status.quote: Applications open November 12, 2026 and are due by 11:59 PM on January 22, 2027

pool.quote: The total amount of funding this year is at least $1 million.

applicant_types.quote: Grants of up to $100,000 are available to land trusts and other non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations with a conservation-related mission, academic institutions, Federally Recognized Tribal Nations

geography.quote: The program geography includes all or portions of Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, West Virginia, Virginia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Georgia and Alabama.

access.quote: The application is completed and submitted through SurveyMonkey's Apply platform.

effort.quote: Applications open November 12, 2026 and close January 22, 2027.
Projects will be evaluated on the following criteria:

eligibility.quote: The program is open to all land trusts and other non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations with a conservation-related mission, non-profit academic institutions, Federally Recognized Tribal Nations (as well as affiliated non-profits applying on their behalf), municipalities and village, town and county agencies that operate within the Appalachians boundary.

Projects must be located in TNC's Appalachians Program boundary which includes portions of Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, West Virginia, Virginia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Georgia or Alabama.
Eligible projects will permanently conserve lands that are within or intersect with the Resilient and Connected Network (RCN) and the program’s focal areas.

the project is within TNC’s Appalachians Program boundary and within a mapped focal area. Projects with outstanding conservation values and compelling community engagement attributes that are outside of but close to a focal area may be considered as funding allows. Please reach out to discuss before applying.

Yes, if they are adjacent to one another and under a single ownership. If they are not adjacent, the project is still eligible so long as they are owned by the same individual(s) or entity and there is a clear conservation relationship between them that promotes landscape connectivity
The earliest a project can close and still be eligible for a grant is April 1, 2027.
Applicants may only submit one application per year.
While projects are required to close within 12 months, the grant term is 18 months, from June 30 through December 31 to allow for any unexpected delays.

documents.quote: Maps and other project-specific attachments Project budget (including budget worksheet and narrative in the application)
The Conflict Inquiry form is required for all non-profit organizations.
Land trusts that are accredited by the Land Trust Accreditation Commission must provide documentation showing that they are and will remain accredited through the start of the grant term.
Letter of Intent for accreditation submitted within the past year (if applicable)
IRS determination letter § Organizational by-laws and articles of incorporation § Most recent Form 990 or Financial Statement § Certificate of Good Standing from State where organization is located
Land trusts that are currently accredited by the Land Trust Accreditation Commission (LTAC) and will maintain their accreditation through 2027 must · upload their current accreditation letter.

after_award.quote: Grantees must send a copy of the recorded deed to Matt Levy at mlevy@tnc.org no later than 60 days from the date of closing.
